title: Bill Calculators for Every DISCO in Pakistan | Wattlyst
meta: A bill calculator for each DISCO: LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, GEPCO, FESCO, PESCO, HESCO, SEPCO, QESCO, TESCO and K-Electric, plus FPA and overbilling checks.
author: ali-ahmad

p: LESCO (Lahore), IESCO (Islamabad and Rawalpindi), MEPCO (Multan and south Punjab), GEPCO (Gujranwala), FESCO (Faisalabad), PESCO (Peshawar), HESCO (Hyderabad), SEPCO (Sukkur), QESCO (Quetta), TESCO (the merged tribal districts) and K-Electric (Karachi) each have their own page with local notes. The electricity bill calculator for Pakistan covers all of them in one place with the fullest explanation of the slabs.

sections.h2: Checks on a bill you already have
p: If a bill looks too high, the overbilling check tests a long reading cycle and the slab it pushed you into, and the Pakistan Bill Index shows the typical bill for your units this month on a 2 kW sanctioned load. The FPA line is explained in the FPA guide and time-of-use rates in the peak hours guide.
Before adding load, the AC bill calculator shows what one more AC adds to the whole bill, and the sanctioned load calculator whether the connection needs a load extension.

faq.q: Is the per unit rate different for LESCO, IESCO and K-Electric?
faq.a: No. All the ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric bill the uniform NEPRA domestic tariff for the year; the monthly fuel adjustment, FPA on most bills and FCA on K-Electric bills, is one national figure too, so the same units give the same bill; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: What is the bill for 300 units?
faq.a: About Rs 14,186 for an unprotected home on a 1 kW connection with the July 2026 FPA pre-filled, of which Rs 9,930 is the energy charge at Rs 33.10 per unit. The electricity bill calculator works out any other number of units.

faq.q: Why is my bill higher than the calculator?
faq.a: The estimate uses the pre-filled FPA unless you enter your bill's, and it cannot see arrears, a late payment surcharge or advance income tax on large bills. Copy the FPA from your bill, and if the reading dates cover more than a month, run the overbilling check.
A home whose last 6 bills were all at or under 200 units, on a connection below 5 kW. Protected homes pay much lower slab rates, and one month over the limit ends the status.

key_facts: An unprotected consumer pays the rate of the slab the monthly total reaches on every unit: 300 units are all charged at Rs 33.10, giving Rs 9,930 in energy charges.
LESCO charges the NEPRA uniform A-1 domestic tariff for 2026, so a LESCO bill for a given number of units is the same as any other DISCO's, FPA included, because NEPRA sets one FPA for every company.

What an AC adds to a Pakistani electricity bill is the bill with the AC minus the bill without it, not the AC's units × one slab rate, because the slab the whole home reaches sets the rate of every unit.
